name: SAB Invest
legal_name: Alawwal Invest Company (SAB Invest), a one-person closed joint stock company
founded: 2008 (CR 1010242378 dated 9 Jan 2008; CMA licence 07077-37 / resolution 1-39-2007 dated 22 Jul 2007; operations began 8 Apr 2008) as Alawwal Invest, the investment arm of Alawwal Bank. SAB Invest brand introduced 4 Apr 2023; the legal name remains Alawwal Invest Company.
ownership_summary: 100% owned by Saudi Awwal Bank (SAB). Paid-up capital SAR 840m (84m shares of SAR 10) at 31 Dec 2025. Through SAB, HSBC Group has an indirect interest (HSBC holds 31% of SAB).
government_link: None direct. Parent SAB's largest shareholders are HSBC Holdings B.V. (31%) and Olayan Saudi Investment Company (20.55%) (see sa-sab).
group_structure: Wholly owned subsidiary of Saudi Awwal Bank (sa-sab). History: Alawwal Invest was Alawwal Bank's investment arm and became SAB's subsidiary after the 2019 SABB-Alawwal merger. In May 2021 it agreed to take over HSBC Saudi Arabia's asset management, retail brokerage and retail margin lending businesses and teams; the transfer completed at the end of 2022. HSBC Saudi Arabia itself was not renamed or absorbed: it remains a separate CMA-licensed investment bank, 51% HSBC Group and 49% SAB (associate). SAB Invest also manages the X-Tech VC fund that SAB consolidates. Double counting: SAB Invest is fully consolidated into SAB and drives SAB's 'Capital markets' segment; never add this record's figures to sa-sab.
footprint: Saudi Arabia. 6 investment centres (3 in the Central region incl. the Riyadh head office, Al Khobar and Al Ahsa in the Eastern region, Jeddah) per the website, checked 12 Oct 2026. Digital access for SAB and non-SAB customers and non-resident foreign investors; international trading via WorldTrader (50+ exchanges).
customer_segments: Retail and affluent investors (including SAB Premier and Private Banking clients referred by SAB), HNW individuals and family offices, corporates and institutions (DPMs, outsourced CIO, Employee Thrift and Investment Plan), endowments, and non-resident foreign investors (digital onboarding launched 2025).
business_lines: Asset management (conventional and Shariah mutual funds, multi-asset funds, DPMs, ETFs, real estate, private credit and VC funds); Global Investment Solutions (global funds, advisory, outsourced CIO); brokerage (Saudi, GCC and international equities, US options, margin lending, securities lending from 2026, ETF market making); wealth management (RM coverage, Employee Thrift and Investment Plan, Save+ savings plan). FY2025 revenue SAR 564.7m: asset management fees 250.3m, brokerage fees 48.3m, special commission income (mainly margin lending) 136.7m, income from clients' money 107.2m.

capabilities.wealth_summary: SAB Invest is the trading name of Alawwal Invest Company, SAB's 100%-owned CMA licensee for dealing, managing, arranging, advising and custody. It was not formerly HSBC Saudi Arabia: it absorbed HSBC Saudi Arabia's asset management, retail brokerage and retail margin lending businesses at the end of 2022, while HSBC Saudi Arabia continues as a separate 49%-SAB-owned investment bank. AUM was SAR 34.18bn at end-2025 (SAR 35.04bn in 2024), with SAR 3.4bn in global products and about SAR 3bn of assets under advisory. FY2025 revenue was SAR 564.7m and net profit SAR 180.2m. 2025 was year three of a 17-initiative 5-year strategy (refreshed in Q4 2025 to run to 2030). In 2025 it replaced its asset-management core system, rolled out a CRM, launched the WorldTrader global brokerage platform and soft-launched a Digital Wealth app with 'MAL - Mustasharak Alawwal', model portfolios rebalanced by a robo engine, open to SAB and non-SAB customers and non-residents. 2026 plans include goal-based investing, AI tools for advisers and distribution through fintechs and digital wallets. In 2026 it added securities lending with J.P. Morgan (June) and a USD Shariah Global Select Equity Fund (August).

private_banking.detail: Private Banking is run by SAB (see sa-sab). SAB Invest's wealth management RMs serve SAB referrals (SAR 4.7bn in 2025 per SAB AR) and executed transactions with HSBC Private Banking in 2025.

asset_management.detail: AUM SAR 34.18bn (31 Dec 2025). Range: conventional and Shariah equity, sukuk/fixed income, Murabaha and money market funds; multi-asset funds; DPMs; ETFs (SAB Invest Saudi Quant ETF, May 2025, adapted from an HSBC model; Hang Seng Hong Kong ETF, Oct 2024); real estate development funds (two exited in 2025 for about SAR 1.4bn; three new funds agreed with SAR 4.8bn combined value); private credit (Global Credit Fund >USD 200m; Tactical Credit Opportunities Fund Oct 2025; MENA multi-strategy private credit fund with SAR 350m initial); Shariah venture income fund with STV; Global Select Equity Fund (USD, from 3 Aug 2026). Seven fund awards in 2025 (Lipper, Sanadeeq).

brokerage.detail: Saudi (Tadawul) and GCC equities via SAB Invest RIA/NetPlus web, mobile apps, phone and branches; international via WorldTrader (50+ exchanges, US options, USD-only funding, no minimum; launched 2025; 'Trader Workstation (TWS)' desktop). Margin lending (receivables SAR 1.65bn). First ETF market maker on the Saudi Exchange. Securities lending with J.P. Morgan as agent from Jun 2026. April 2025 Argaam ranking: 12th, 2.8% share. Brokerage fee income fell 18% in 2025 to SAR 48.3m. 2026 plan: core brokerage system upgrade, securities borrowing and lending, WorldTrader margin, short selling and stock yield enhancement.

digital_investing.detail: Apps: 'SAB Invest' (seller Alawwal Invest Company; first iOS release 31 Dec 2025; describes 'mutual fund investment all in one digital channel'), SAB Invest Trade, WorldTrader and WorldTrader Pro; web: SAB Invest Online (account opening and fund subscription without branch visit), SAB Invest Trade, WorldTrader. Board report: new Digital Wealth app with MAL robo/model portfolios, accessible to SAB and non-SAB customers and non-resident foreign investors via open banking; first fully digital non-resident onboarding journey in Saudi (2025).

advisory.detail: CMA advising licence. Global Investment Solutions provides portfolio advisory and Outsourced CIO services for HNW and institutional clients; assets under advisory surpassed SAR 2.9bn at end-2025. 2026 plan: AI and analytics tools for front-line advisers (next best action).

discretionary.detail: Discretionary Portfolio Management (DPMs) for HNW, affluent, corporate and institutional clients, customised per client; no published minimum. Management fees from DPMs are part of asset management fees (FS note 23). DPM AUM not separately disclosed.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: 'MAL - Mustasharak Alawwal' in the new Digital Wealth app: one-off or systematic investment into model portfolios managed by SAB Invest portfolio managers, automatically rebalanced to the chosen risk profile by a robo engine. Board report says the wealth platform was 'soft-launched' in 2025 with a robo-advisory risk-based journey as the initial release. The public App Store description mentions only mutual fund investment, so client-facing MAL availability is not confirmed on public pages.

funds_platform.detail: Distributes own funds via app, online, investment centres and SAB. No third-party fund shelf found. 2026 plan: distribute SAB Invest products through third parties such as fintechs and digital wallets; listing flagship funds with HSBC's booking centre to reach foreign investors.

structured_products.detail: The About page lists structured products among asset management capabilities (S3), but no structured product is published. 'Save+' is a recurring savings plan with returns described as 'up to 5%', not described as a structured product (S14).

private_markets.detail: Real estate development funds (Riyadh office and mixed-use projects), regional and global private credit funds, venture income fund with STV supported by NTDP, X-Tech VC fund, and a partnership with Stride Ventures (Oct 2025, seen in search results only). First MENA private credit strategy for clients raised over SAR 350m in its first round.

islamic_wealth.detail: Shariah Committee; Shariah-compliant equity, sukuk and Murabaha, multi-asset and global credit funds; Saudi Quant ETF is Shariah-compliant; Global Select Equity Fund benchmarked to the S&P Global BMI Shariah index. Conventional products also offered.

discrepancies.detail: Internal notes said SAB Invest was 'formerly HSBC Saudi Arabia'. SAB's H1 2026 FS lists 'Alawwal Invest Company (SAB Invest)' as a 100% subsidiary and HSBC Saudi Arabia separately as a 49% associate. SAB Invest acquired only HSBC Saudi Arabia's asset management, retail brokerage and retail margin lending businesses (end-2022).
discrepancies.resolution: Lead corrected: SAB Invest = renamed Alawwal Invest. HSBC Saudi Arabia still exists.

discrepancies.detail: Board report 2025 lists Osama Alowedi as CIO; the official page (Oct 2026) lists Sultan Alsharqi as CIO (Acting). EnterpriseAM (3 Aug 2026) reported Alowedi's departure citing unnamed sources.
discrepancies.resolution: Alowedi recorded as Departed; acting CIO recorded from the official page.

discrepancies.detail: Audited FS: SAR 2,803,692k. Board report five-year table: SAR 2,803,714k.
FS: SAR 34.18bn vs 35.04bn (-2.5%). Chairman: 'remained stable'. Parent AR: SAR 30.7bn ex-GIS 'declined by 6%'. Board report asset management section calls SAR 30.7bn 'a record'.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded audited FS total. Statements about direction conflict; the SAR 30.7bn ex-GIS figure is not recorded as AUM.

discrepancies.detail: About page says 'established on 27th Dhu Al-Hijjah 1428, 1st January 2008'; FS and board report give CR date 30 Dhul Hijjah 1428H = 9 Jan 2008.
Board reports 2021-2023 list Khalid Al-Mulhem as Chairman, Non-Executive; the 2025 board report lists him as Chairman, Independent. The official board page gives no classification.
discrepancies.resolution: Title recorded as on the official page ('Chairman of the Board'); classification left unresolved. Minor.

discrepancies.detail: The 2025 board report titles Mohammed Tajammul 'Head of Information Technology', Jean-Philippe Gariazzo 'Head of Strategy & Transformation', Ayman Al Hassan 'Head of Finance' and Fawaz AlSadhan 'Head of Legal'; the management page (Oct 2026) says Chief Technology Officer, Chief Strategy and Transformation Officer, Chief Finance Officer and Chief Legal Officer.
discrepancies.resolution: Website titles used (more recent); report titles kept in appointed_note. Minor.

discrepancies.detail: The earlier file said he headed IT 'from 2016'. The official page says that in 2016 he moved to Alawwal Bank as Programme Manager (IT delivery and the Alawwal-SABB IT integration) and that in 2022 he was appointed to lead and establish the IT function for SAB Invest.
Website: 9 years based in Saudi Arabia; board report 2025: 8 years (2006-2009 and 2017 to date).

Whether the MAL robo/model-portfolio journey is fully live to the public (board report says 'soft-launched'; App Store text mentions only mutual funds).
